source_review.notes: Checked all six current official sources. The September 2025 specification supports request-versus-execution error distinction, field collection, response-name grouping, normal and serial execution, recursive value completion, abstract/list/non-null behavior, response paths, partial data, and error propagation. Current GraphQL execution, response, performance, and HTTP guides support resolver/context/request-pipeline boundaries. The GraphQL Foundation DataLoader reference supports per-request construction, exact positional/cardinality batch results, scheduling windows, memoization, error behavior, invalidation, duplicate-key caveats, and maximum batch size.

evidence: Checked O, response graph G_O=(P,E), response position p, coordinate f(p), resolver r_f, completion function, n, K, m, u, b, Y, q, d, and c for consistent domains.
Confirmed ceiling, cardinality, unique-key, index-correspondence, ordered-list, and context-equivalence notation agrees with prose.
Confirmed execution, collected field set, resolver, value completion, response path, N+1, batch loader, request memoization, and batch window are explicitly defined.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation separates GraphQL response structure, implementation functions, backend-call arithmetic, scheduling, and visibility equivalence.

evidence: Recomputed 100 parents and 60 unique keys at cap 25 as 101 naive calls versus 1+ceil(60/25)=4 batched calls.
Recomputed Exercise 2 as 241 naive calls versus 1+ceil(83/30)=4 batched calls.
Checked the executable alignment example has four input slots, preserves duplicate key 9, represents missing key 6, and reports equal length.
Counted ten distinct worked examples and five exercise-answer pairs.
numerical_recomputation.notes: All numerical claims are exact examples or identities; no production performance result is asserted.

evidence: Derived 1+ceil(u/b) from one parent call and a partition of u unique keys into batches no larger than b.
Verified map-over-original-keys yields output cardinality and positional correspondence even when backend rows reorder or omit keys.
Constructed differing-visibility requests with equal raw IDs to show a cache key that omits visibility can substitute an unauthorized value.
Checked side effects in normally executed siblings make behavior schedule-dependent, while idempotent side-effect-free fields remove that dependency.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Proofs are bounded by compatible key semantics, loader/library behavior, backend identity, and stated execution-mode assumptions.

evidence: Reviewed fragments, aliases, directives, repeated fields, abstract types, empty/null lists, non-null propagation, async reordering, mutation-root order, and partial data.
Reviewed zero/one/max/over-max batches, duplicates with cache on/off, unordered/sparse rows, per-key and whole-batch errors, scheduler delay, cancellation, deadlines, and sub-batch concurrency.

Reviewed concurrent tenant/principal same IDs, policy/snapshot/locale/projection variants, mutation invalidation, transient error caching, immutable values, loader lifecycle, telemetry cardinality, and secret leakage.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Coverage spans language execution, concurrency, data identity, consistency, security, failure granularity, resources, and observability.

evidence: The batch-key-alignment program checks backend reordering, duplicate preservation, explicit missing value, and exact output length.
Confirmed only validated/coerced operations enter execution and ordinary fields remain side-effect-free/idempotent under normal scheduling.
Confirmed per-request context and loaders preserve visibility scope, deadline/cancellation, bounded batches, immutable memoized values, and mutation invalidation.
Confirmed execution errors retain response-position semantics and declared null wrappers determine propagation.
invariant_checking.notes: The local model demonstrates alignment only; runtime scheduling, authentication, persistence, cancellation, and backend bounds require integration evidence.

evidence: Reviewed N+1 reduction proof and confirmed its omissions—deeper waves, bytes, retries, and concurrency—are stated.
Reviewed positional mapping proof and confirmed it produces one slot per original occurrence rather than per unique backend row.
Reviewed request-isolation counterexample and confirmed different visibility with equal raw key refutes unsafe cross-request reuse.
Reviewed normal-versus-serial reasoning and confirmed root mutation order is not overstated as transactionality.
proof_review.notes: Arguments are logically valid and their protocol, implementation, and operational assumptions are explicit.

evidence: Confirmed specification-required execution behavior is separated from common resolver-library interfaces and DataLoader implementation behavior.
Confirmed call-count formulas are labeled local models rather than latency or capacity guarantees.
Confirmed request memoization is separated from shared caching, root serialization from transactions, and cancellation from rollback.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Normative GraphQL behavior, common framework mechanism, local design policy, mathematical model, and empirical claim remain distinguishable.

evidence: Current official claims record a 2026-09-02 retrieval date and six checked sources.
Snippet verification is required to reproduce the deterministic batch alignment example before promotion.

Actual resolver order, dependency calls/bytes, batch distribution, cache isolation, null behavior, cancellation, pool pressure, latency, and telemetry leakage remain deployment-specific evidence obligations.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No production GraphQL executor, client corpus, loader library configuration, datastore, or workload was empirically assessed.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed the complete flow from validated operation through field collection, normal/serial resolution, value completion, N+1 diagnosis, aligned request-scoped batching, consistency/invalidation, error propagation, observability, and verification with pagination and authorization/cost boundaries preserved.

practitioner_review.notes: Checked implementability through request context factories, narrow resolver adapters, domain ports, per-request loaders, composite semantic keys, exact batch mapping, caps/partitioning/concurrency, commit-aware invalidation, cancellation, bounded coordinate telemetry, oracle/property/integration/load tests, and cleanup assertions.

pedagogical_review.notes: The module follows actual execution order, then exposes amplification and repairs it with a precise positional/security model. The executable example is small and bounded; ten cases are distinct; five exercises progress from definitions and arithmetic to an emergency coordination synthesis with complete answers.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
